newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ dollar corrects up to close with fragile gains.
newsitem.headline: NZ dollar corrects up to close with fragile gains.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar ended a thin session holding on to its early gains after the traumas of Friday's plunge, but dealers said the modesty of the kiwi's rebound suggested it would face further downward pressure soon.
By 5.30 p.m. (0530 GMT) it was trading at 0.6528/35 to the U.S. dollar, just ahead of its 0.6524/31 open, but well short of its weekend highs of 0.6560 when U.S. demand was seen.
"There was quite a bit of two-way interest, but we're probably seeing a technical correction," a senior Wellington dealer said.
The Trade Weighted Index ended at 64.64 after a 64.56 start.
Dealers said the market had been fairly illiquid, and many market players had been feeling too unsure of the prospects to enter the fray, prefering to wait and see.
"However, the market is very short, and given that it's so short I think the fact that it hasn't rallied far could be a pointer to further downside risk," another dealer added.

Traders felt that there would have to be a considerable head of steam on the buy-side before any significantly higher levels beyond 0.6450 might be regained and as this was not apparent, further softening looked more likely.

Australian inflation and jobs data on the horizon for later this week could provide a new lead, with Australian interest rates still seen having potential to fall, but otherwise new local factors looked few and far between, dealers said.
